description: Eight equivalence states for comparing function representations, from weakest to strongest

SYNTACTIC_MATCH.definition: String or AST representation is identical
SYNTACTIC_MATCH.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent (syntax match alone does not imply behavioral equivalence)

SPECIFICATION_MATCH.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent (specification match does not imply implementation equivalence)

FINITE_TEST_BEHAVIOR_MATCH.definition: Functions produce identical outputs on a finite test set
FINITE_TEST_BEHAVIOR_MATCH.check_method: Run both on test suite and compare outputs
FINITE_TEST_BEHAVIOR_MATCH.allowed_claim: These functions match on the tested inputs
FINITE_TEST_BEHAVIOR_MATCH.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent (finite testing cannot prove equivalence)

DISTRIBUTIONAL_APPROXIMATION.definition: Functions produce statistically similar output distributions
DISTRIBUTIONAL_APPROXIMATION.check_method: Statistical test (KS test, Wasserstein distance, etc.)
DISTRIBUTIONAL_APPROXIMATION.allowed_claim: These functions have similar output distributions
DISTRIBUTIONAL_APPROXIMATION.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent (distributional similarity is not equivalence)

OBSERVATIONAL_EQUIVALENCE.definition: No observable difference exists between functions under defined observation model
OBSERVATIONAL_EQUIVALENCE.allowed_claim: These functions are observationally equivalent under the defined model
OBSERVATIONAL_EQUIVALENCE.forbidden_claim: These functions are semantically equivalent (observational equivalence is model-dependent)

FORMAL_SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE.definition: Functions are provably equivalent under formal denotational or operational semantics
FORMAL_SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE.allowed_claim: These functions are formally semantically equivalent
FORMAL_SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE.forbidden_claim: This equivalence extends beyond the formalized semantic domain

EMPIRICAL_PERFORMANCE_SIMILARITY.definition: Functions achieve similar performance on empirical benchmarks
EMPIRICAL_PERFORMANCE_SIMILARITY.allowed_claim: These functions have similar empirical performance
EMPIRICAL_PERFORMANCE_SIMILARITY.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent (performance similarity is not functional equivalence)

NOT_COMPARABLE.definition: Functions use different representations or domains that prevent comparison
NOT_COMPARABLE.check_method: Check if comparison methods are applicable
NOT_COMPARABLE.allowed_claim: These functions are not comparable with available methods
NOT_COMPARABLE.forbidden_claim: These functions are equivalent or non-equivalent (no claim can be made)

transition_rules.SYNTACTIC_MATCH → SPECIFICATION_MATCH: Automatic if specifications are extracted from syntax
transition_rules.FINITE_TEST_BEHAVIOR_MATCH → DISTRIBUTIO: Requires statistical analysis on larger sample

forbidden_transitions: Cannot skip from SYNTACTIC_MATCH directly to FORMAL_SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE
Cannot claim FORMAL_SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENCE from EMPIRICAL_PERFORMANCE_SIMILARITY alone
